questions.stem: A Helena student turns 18 next week and requests a Montana commission today. Which qualification is missing?
options: Ownership of real estate
Attaining age 18
A university diploma
Five years of employment
questions.explanation: The individual must be at least 18 to hold the commission.
feedback: Real-estate ownership is not the age qualification.
Correct. The individual must be at least 18 to hold the commission.
A diploma is not a listed condition.
That employment period is not stated.

questions.stem: A permanent legal resident living in Great Falls is told only United States citizens qualify. How should she assess that advice?
options: Permanent legal residency satisfies the status alternative
Only natural-born citizens qualify
Any foreign passport establishes every qualification
A tourist visa always qualifies
questions.explanation: The statute permits citizens or permanent legal residents of the United States.
feedback: Correct. The statute permits citizens or permanent legal residents of the United States.
The section does not require natural-born citizenship.
A passport does not establish all appointment conditions.
The statutory alternative is permanent legal residency.

questions.stem: An Idaho resident regularly works at a registered and licensed employer's Missoula office and meets the other qualifications. Which connection can support her application?
options: Ownership of a home in every Montana county
A client's promise to hire her
Attendance at a Montana concert
Qualifying Montana employment
questions.explanation: Regular employment at the specified Montana office is a residency alternative.
feedback: Multiple home ownership is not required.
A client's future promise does not establish the listed employment.
Attendance at an event is not a listed connection.
Correct. Regular employment at the specified Montana office is a residency alternative.

questions.stem: A nonresident opens a Montana business but skips its required registration and local licensing. What must be resolved before relying on the business alternative?
options: A law degree for every owner
A requirement to operate only online
The specified registration and licensing requirements
A mandatory 100-person staff
questions.explanation: The business connection requires Title 35 registration and applicable local licensing.
feedback: The alternative does not require a law degree.
Online-only operation is not the qualification.
Correct. The business connection requires Title 35 registration and applicable local licensing.
The statute sets no 100-person staff requirement.

questions.stem: A nonresident holds a current professional license issued by the appropriate Montana authority. What can that license establish?
options: Permission to use an expired notary stamp
A listed Montana-connection alternative
Automatic issuance of a notary commission
An exemption from all education and examination
questions.explanation: Current qualifying Montana professional licensure is one connection route.
feedback: Professional licensure does not extend an expired commission.
Correct. Current qualifying Montana professional licensure is one connection route.
A separate notary application remains necessary.
The other commissioning requirements remain.

questions.stem: A legal dependent of military personnel assigned to active duty in Montana retains another state's residence. Which eligibility fact matters?
options: The military-dependent connection is expressly listed
Every military relative is automatically commissioned
The dependent must personally enlist first
Only property ownership supplies a connection
questions.explanation: A spouse or legal dependent of personnel assigned to active duty in Montana has a statutory connection alternative.
feedback: Correct. A spouse or legal dependent of personnel assigned to active duty in Montana has a statutory connection alternative.
The connection does not itself issue a commission.
The dependent's enlistment is not this alternative.
The statute provides several geographic alternatives.

questions.stem: An applicant cannot read or write English and proposes that a friend translate every notarial task. Which individual qualification remains?
options: A degree in translation
Ability to speak every client's language
An employer's recommendation
Ability to read and write English
questions.explanation: The applicant must personally satisfy the English reading and writing qualification.
feedback: A translation degree is not stated.
Universal language proficiency is not listed.
An employer's recommendation does not supply the missing ability.
Correct. The applicant must personally satisfy the English reading and writing qualification.

questions.stem: An applicant buys personal liability insurance and asks to omit Montana's prescribed assurance. What is required?
options: A client's liability waiver
No assurance after an exam pass
A $25,000 surety bond or qualifying functional equivalent
Any insurance regardless of terms
questions.explanation: The prescribed assurance must satisfy the statutory amount, issuer and form conditions.
feedback: Client waivers do not replace the assurance.
Passing an examination does not remove the bond condition.
Correct. The prescribed assurance must satisfy the statutory amount, issuer and form conditions.
An arbitrary insurance policy need not satisfy those conditions.

questions.stem: A company unauthorized to do business in Montana offers a cheap notary assurance. Which issuer condition must the applicant verify?
options: That the employer bought it
Montana licensing or authorization to do business
That the issuer is the applicant's bank
That the issuer has a Helena storefront
questions.explanation: The assurance issuer must be licensed or authorized to do business in Montana.
feedback: Who pays does not establish the issuer's authority.
Correct. The assurance issuer must be licensed or authorized to do business in Montana.
A bank-only issuer rule is not stated.
The statute does not require that storefront.

questions.stem: A notary's assurance is canceled while the commission certificate still has two years remaining. What governs continued acts?
options: Valid assurance must remain on file
The printed expiration date alone is sufficient
Clients may waive the assurance
Authority continues until the next tax year
questions.explanation: Performance in Montana is permitted only while valid assurance is on file.
feedback: Correct. Performance in Montana is permitted only while valid assurance is on file.
A remaining certificate term does not supply valid assurance.
Client consent does not waive this requirement.
The section supplies no tax-year extension.

questions.stem: A notary wants separate Montana commissions for bank work and weekend business. What limitation applies?
options: Every employer needs a separate employee commission
A second county requires another commission
Buying another stamp creates another commission
One individual cannot hold concurrent Montana commissions
questions.explanation: An individual may have only one Montana notary commission in effect at a time.
feedback: A commission is issued to the individual.
A county change does not require concurrent commissions.
Supplies do not create appointment authority.
Correct. An individual may have only one Montana notary commission in effect at a time.

questions.stem: An applicant buys an eight-year insurance policy and expects an eight-year Montana commission. What term does the section establish?
options: Lifetime authority
One year per premium payment
Four years
Eight years
questions.explanation: The statutory commission term is four years.
feedback: This provision does not grant lifetime authority.
Premium payments do not calculate the term.
Correct. The statutory commission term is four years.
Insurance duration does not set the commission term.

questions.stem: The bond bears an applicant's official name, but her Montana online application uses another name. What should she resolve?
options: Ask a client to choose the commissioned name
Make the application name exactly match the bond
Use either name because the photo matches
Leave the application name blank
questions.explanation: The SOS filing instructions require the application and bond names to match exactly.
feedback: Clients do not select the applicant's filing identity.
Correct. The SOS filing instructions require the application and bond names to match exactly.
Photo familiarity does not waive the filing instruction.
An incomplete application does not resolve the discrepancy.
questions.reference: Online application — matching application and bond names

questions.stem: A Montana applicant has certificates and a bond form but proposes signing its oath privately at home. What procedure does the SOS describe?
options: Execute the oath before another notary
Notarize the applicant's own oath
Replace the oath with an unsigned witness email
Skip the oath after passing the examination
questions.explanation: The standardized bond includes a statement and oath executed before another notary.
feedback: Correct. The standardized bond includes a statement and oath executed before another notary.
Self-notarization does not supply a valid applicant oath.
An unsigned email does not administer the oath.
The examination does not replace the oath.
questions.reference: Obtain a notary surety bond — statement and oath

questions.stem: An applicant answers yes to a reportable Montana background question and leaves the explanation blank. What do the filing instructions require?
options: A second stamp
A higher examination score
Waiting until a complaint arrives
The specified explanatory documentation
questions.explanation: Specified affirmative background answers require supporting explanation documents.
feedback: A stamp does not explain the background answer.
An exam score does not replace disclosure.
The filing instruction applies at application.
Correct. Specified affirmative background answers require supporting explanation documents.

questions.stem: A Montana applicant intentionally conceals an out-of-state suspension in the application. Which commissioning consequence is supported?
options: Payment guarantees approval
Only a criminal conviction can support action
The deceitful omission can support denial or discipline
Filing automatically erases the suspension
questions.explanation: A fraudulent or deceitful application omission is a statutory ground for commissioning action.
feedback: Payment does not immunize the application.
The listed grounds extend beyond criminal convictions.
Correct. A fraudulent or deceitful application omission is a statutory ground for commissioning action.
The application does not erase disciplinary history.

questions.stem: An applicant with restored full rights asks whether a past conviction is automatically an absolute lifetime bar under this provision. What is accurate?
options: Only the bond company decides appointment
The statute says restored full rights prevent the conviction from being a complete bar
Approval is automatic after one day
The SOS may never consider conduct
questions.explanation: The section recognizes restored rights while retaining the other eligibility and integrity grounds.
feedback: Commissioning belongs to the SOS.
Correct. The section recognizes restored rights while retaining the other eligibility and integrity grounds.
The statute does not promise automatic approval.
Other integrity-related grounds remain relevant.

questions.stem: During a Montana commission, a notary pleads no contest to a felony involving deceit. What reporting period applies?
options: Notify the SOS within 30 days
Wait until the next renewal
Notify only the employer
Report only after a client complaint
questions.explanation: Notice is required within 30 days of the specified conviction or plea.
feedback: Correct. Notice is required within 30 days of the specified conviction or plea.
Renewal does not replace timely reporting.
The statute requires notice to the SOS.
A complaint is not the reporting trigger.

questions.stem: The SOS proposes conditions on a Montana commission after misconduct. Which procedural right does the section recognize?
options: An automatic pardon after buying a bond
An unconditional right to continue forever
A client vote overriding the SOS
Contesting the action under the Montana Administrative Procedure Act
questions.explanation: The section provides a statutory procedure for contesting specified commissioning actions.
feedback: A new bond does not erase proposed discipline.
The statute permits commission conditions.
Clients do not adjudicate the commission.
Correct. The section provides a statutory procedure for contesting specified commissioning actions.

questions.stem: A Montana notary violates an official notary rule and claims only statutes can support discipline. What does the section provide?
options: Only paid acts are regulated
Rules apply only before appointment
A notary-rule violation is a listed ground
Rules never affect commissioned notaries
questions.explanation: A violation of an SOS rule governing notaries can support commissioning action.
feedback: The ground is not limited to paid work.
The section applies during commissioned service.
Correct. A violation of an SOS rule governing notaries can support commissioning action.
The statute expressly includes applicable rules.

questions.stem: A Kalispell customer cannot explain the document and the notary remains unsatisfied about capacity. What is required?
options: Ask for a waiver of capacity requirements
Refuse while the required capacity determination cannot be made
Rely solely on a relative's reassurance
Proceed for a higher fee
questions.explanation: The officer must be satisfied that the individual is competent or has capacity to execute the record.
feedback: The section does not authorize that waiver.
Correct. The officer must be satisfied that the individual is competent or has capacity to execute the record.
A relative cannot replace the notary's determination.
Compensation does not cure the concern.

questions.stem: A manager answers every question and prevents the signer from speaking freely. A Montana notary remains unsatisfied about voluntary execution. What follows?
options: Refuse until the required determination can be made
Rely only on the manager's instruction
Complete an undated certificate
Proceed without charging
questions.explanation: The officer must refuse when unsatisfied about knowing or voluntary execution.
feedback: Correct. The officer must refuse when unsatisfied about knowing or voluntary execution.
The manager cannot supply the signer's voluntariness.
An undated certificate does not cure the concern.
Free service has the same substantive requirement.

questions.stem: A Montana non-attorney notary advertises that she will choose the legal terms of customers' trusts. What authority is missing?
options: Permission to use two stamps
Permission to advertise in English
Permission to charge the notarial-act fee
Authority to draft legal records or give legal advice
questions.explanation: A notary commission does not authorize drafting legal records or practicing law.
feedback: Two stamps do not confer legal-practice authority.
Advertising language does not create a law license.
The notarial fee does not include unauthorized legal services.
Correct. A notary commission does not authorize drafting legal records or practicing law.

questions.stem: A Montana non-attorney proposes a Spanish advertisement headed notario publico. Which restriction applies?
options: Translation software authorizes the title
A fee under $10 authorizes the title
The term is restricted to a notary also licensed as a Montana attorney
The term is mandatory in every Spanish advertisement
questions.explanation: Montana restricts notario and notario publico terminology by non-attorney notaries.
feedback: Software does not supply attorney licensure.
The act-fee cap does not remove the title restriction.
Correct. Montana restricts notario and notario publico terminology by non-attorney notaries.
The statute restricts that terminology.

questions.stem: A Montana notary holds a client's original contract solely to force payment of an unrelated debt. What issue arises?
options: Automatic ownership by the notary
Improper withholding of the client's original record
A blanket notarial lien on every original
A duty to keep all original contracts for ten years
questions.explanation: Except as otherwise allowed by law, the notary may not withhold access to or retain the client's original record.
feedback: Notarization does not transfer ownership.
Correct. Except as otherwise allowed by law, the notary may not withhold access to or retain the client's original record.
The commission does not create that blanket lien.
Journal retention does not require retaining every original.

questions.stem: A Montana applicant receives 79% on the official examination. How should she treat that result?
options: Below the stated passing threshold
Passing because it rounds to 80
Passing if a bond has been purchased
A commission effective immediately
questions.explanation: The SOS states that 80% is the passing grade.
feedback: Correct. The SOS states that 80% is the passing grade.
The instruction does not authorize that rounding rule.
Purchasing a bond does not change the grade.
An exam result does not itself grant a commission.
questions.reference: Take and pass the Montana notary exam — 80% threshold

questions.stem: An applicant passed Montana's exam eight months before submitting her application. Which timing condition is unmet?
options: The pass must be at least one year old
Every passing score lasts four years
Scores are valid for life
The pass must be no more than six months before application
questions.explanation: The SOS requires a new or renewing applicant's pass within the six months before submission.
feedback: The instruction imposes a maximum age, not a one-year wait.
The commission term does not establish score validity.
Passing scores have a stated recency requirement.
Correct. The SOS requires a new or renewing applicant's pass within the six months before submission.
questions.reference: Take and pass the Montana notary exam — six-month recency

questions.stem: A Montana examinee has failed two attempts and asks whether the three-month waiting rule already applies solely from those two failures. Which reading matches the instruction?
options: It applies only to renewal applicants
A bond company selects the trigger
It is triggered after three unsuccessful attempts
It begins after the first incorrect answer
questions.explanation: The published waiting rule follows three failed attempts.
feedback: The instruction covers both new and renewing applicants.
The official instruction supplies the trigger.
Correct. The published waiting rule follows three failed attempts.
A single incorrect answer is not the stated trigger.
questions.reference: Take and pass the Montana notary exam — three attempts

questions.stem: An examinee wants to study only stamp shopping and ignore Montana notary ethics. What does the examination's statutory course basis include?
options: Only the examiner's personal preferences
Laws, rules, procedures and ethics relevant to notarial acts
Only retail prices
Only county geography
questions.explanation: The examination is based on the course covering those four substantive areas.
feedback: The statute supplies a subject basis.
Correct. The examination is based on the course covering those four substantive areas.
Retail prices are not the full statutory curriculum.
County geography alone omits the statutory subjects.

questions.stem: A first-time applicant completed an approved four-hour Montana course 15 months before applying. Which requirement needs attention?
options: Education must have been completed within the previous 12 months
Education is valid indefinitely after payment
Education must be exactly four years old
An employer can waive the education timing
questions.explanation: Initial education must include at least four approved hours within the preceding 12 months.
feedback: Correct. Initial education must include at least four approved hours within the preceding 12 months.
Payment does not extend the statutory education window.
Four years is the commission term rather than the required course age.
An employer cannot waive the timing condition.

questions.stem: A vendor advertises four hours of notary videos without approval by either designated Montana authority. What must the applicant verify?
options: Only that the vendor uses the word official
Only that the videos cost money
Only that a coworker recommends them
Approval by the SOS or commission of continuing legal education
questions.explanation: The statute identifies the authorities whose education approval qualifies.
feedback: A marketing label does not establish approval.
A purchase does not establish approval.
A recommendation does not supply official approval.
Correct. The statute identifies the authorities whose education approval qualifies.

questions.stem: An applicant deletes the Montana exam certificate after seeing the passing screen. Why is obtaining a usable copy important?
options: It authorizes another person's use of the stamp
It eliminates the filing fee
The online application requires exam completion evidence
The certificate replaces the applicant's oath
questions.explanation: The SOS instructs applicants to retain the examination certificate as an application document.
feedback: A certificate does not permit stamp delegation.
Evidence of passing does not remove the fee.
Correct. The SOS instructs applicants to retain the examination certificate as an application document.
The oath remains a separate requirement.
questions.reference: Training and examination certificates — upload requirements

questions.stem: A first-time applicant passes the Montana exam without completing approved education. Does passing alone satisfy both prerequisites?
options: Yes, if the application is electronic
No, the approved education requirement is additional
Yes, passing automatically creates education credit
Yes, if the score is perfect
questions.explanation: The statute requires approved education in addition to passing the examination.
feedback: Electronic filing does not waive the course.
Correct. The statute requires approved education in addition to passing the examination.
The statute does not automatically convert a pass into course credit.
A perfect score does not waive the separate course.

questions.stem: A Montana practice website claims its own item count is the official state examination count. The opened official gateway does not confirm the count. What should the learner do?
options: Treat the website's count as a practice setting unless official support is found
Assume every practice count is official
Use the number of purchased flashcards as the official count
Ignore the official examination gateway
questions.explanation: An unsupported practice configuration should not be represented as an official examination specification.
feedback: Correct. An unsupported practice configuration should not be represented as an official examination specification.
Private practice settings do not establish official specifications.
Flashcard totals do not establish exam length.
The official gateway remains the appropriate examination entry.
questions.reference: Official examination gateway and published specifications

questions.stem: An applicant uploads a vendor receipt instead of certification of passing the exam and completing education. Which distinction matters?
options: Any receipt proves an exam pass
A receipt establishes a four-year commission
A receipt removes the need to apply
Payment evidence does not necessarily establish successful completion
questions.explanation: The application requires certification of examination success and education completion.
feedback: Purchasing a course does not prove passing.
A receipt is not the commission certificate.
The applicant must still file the required application.
Correct. The application requires certification of examination success and education completion.

questions.stem: A renewing notary completed four approved continuing-education hours during the previous 12 months. Which education route does this fit?
options: The initial applicant's bond exemption
The three-year alternative without yearly hours
The four-hour recent-education alternative
A lifetime exemption
questions.explanation: Renewal education may be four approved continuing hours within the preceding 12 months.
feedback: Education does not create a bond exemption.
This fact pattern uses the recent four-hour alternative.
Correct. Renewal education may be four approved continuing hours within the preceding 12 months.
The statute still imposes future renewal requirements.

questions.stem: A renewing Montana notary has six continuing-education hours concentrated in one year and none in the other two preceding years. What must she avoid assuming?
options: That approval of education matters
That the total alone satisfies the two-hours-in-each-year alternative
That an education certificate can document course completion
That the recent-four-hour alternative should be checked separately
questions.explanation: The three-year alternative requires at least two hours in each preceding year.
feedback: Approval remains part of the statutory condition.
Correct. The three-year alternative requires at least two hours in each preceding year.
Certificates can provide relevant evidence.
A qualifying recent-four-hour route remains a separate possibility.

questions.stem: A renewing Montana notary completed continuing education and asks to skip the exam because she already passed four years earlier. What applies?
options: Renewed commissions also require passing the examination
Every renewal is automatically exam-exempt
Only a name change triggers an exam
The bond company can waive the state exam
questions.explanation: Section 1-5-620 applies the examination requirement to new and renewed commissions.
feedback: Correct. Section 1-5-620 applies the examination requirement to new and renewed commissions.
The statute includes renewed commissions.
The requirement is not limited to name changes.
A bond company does not waive the statutory prerequisite.

questions.stem: A notary tries to file a Montana renewal 60 days before expiration. What does the online filing guidance say?
options: The window opens two years before expiration
Every renewal must be filed after expiration
The system accepts renewal at any time
The renewal window opens 30 days before expiration
questions.explanation: The SOS portal limits the advance renewal window to 30 days.
feedback: The guidance states a much shorter advance window.
Timely pre-expiration filing is permitted.
The portal has a stated timing window.
Correct. The SOS portal limits the advance renewal window to 30 days.

questions.stem: A Montana notary is 40 days beyond commission expiration and attempts the portal's renewal procedure. Which published limit is relevant?
options: The old stamp extends the grace period
A client may grant another month
The stated renewal grace window ends 30 days after expiration
Every expired commission renews automatically
questions.explanation: The SOS portal does not permit renewal after its stated 30-day grace period.
feedback: A physical stamp does not extend the window.
Clients do not set commissioning deadlines.
Correct. The SOS portal does not permit renewal after its stated 30-day grace period.
Expiration does not trigger automatic renewal.
questions.reference: Online filing renewal window — thirty-day grace period

questions.stem: A notary submits a Montana renewal and plans to act after the current term ends while approval is pending. Which authority must be established?
options: A promise to backdate the next certificate
A current effective commission and valid assurance
Submission alone
The employer's deadline
questions.explanation: A renewal application does not by itself extend the expiring commission's authority.
feedback: Backdating cannot supply authority during a gap.
Correct. A renewal application does not by itself extend the expiring commission's authority.
Filing does not itself issue a new commission.
An employer cannot extend public authority.

questions.stem: After renewal, a notary still has a stamp showing the old expiration date. What must happen to that expired-date device?
options: Render it unusable as required
Keep using it until its ink runs out
Loan it to a newly commissioned colleague
Erase the date on completed certificates
questions.explanation: Expiration of the date shown in the device triggers its disabling requirement.
feedback: Correct. Expiration of the date shown in the device triggers its disabling requirement.
Ink remaining does not extend a device's valid date.
Another person may not use the notary's device.
Alterations to completed stamp images are not the remedy.

questions.stem: A surety tells a renewing Montana notary that cancellation of the assurance never needs advance SOS notice. What does the statute state?
options: Only the client must be notified
Notice is optional if the premium was late
Notice waits until the next renewal
The issuer must give 30 days' notice before cancellation
questions.explanation: The assurance issuer must give the SOS 30 days' notice before cancellation.
feedback: Client notice is not the specified SOS notice.
The stated notice rule does not provide that premium exception.
The statute requires notice before cancellation.
Correct. The assurance issuer must give the SOS 30 days' notice before cancellation.

questions.stem: A surety pays a claimant on a Montana notary assurance. What reporting obligation does the statute place on the issuer?
options: Wait for a later journal request
Destroy the claimant's records
Notify the SOS within 30 days after payment
Issue the notary a second commission
questions.explanation: The issuer must report the payment to the SOS within 30 days.
feedback: A journal request is not the payment-reporting trigger.
The statute does not direct destruction of records.
Correct. The issuer must report the payment to the SOS within 30 days.
The surety cannot issue a commission.

questions.stem: An applicant asks when the complete Montana application package must relate to the bond effective date or prior commission expiration. Which statutory window applies?
options: Only after a customer requests service
Within 30 days before or after the relevant specified date
At any point during the next four years
Only on the final business day of the year
questions.explanation: The section links submission to the stated 30-day window around the bond date or prior expiration.
feedback: Customer demand does not set the filing window.
Correct. The section links submission to the stated 30-day window around the bond date or prior expiration.
The commission term does not supply an unrestricted filing window.
The section has no year-end-only requirement.

questions.stem: Another state refuses to renew an individual's notary commission. When the person seeks Montana renewal, how may that history matter?
options: It is a listed potential ground for Montana action
It must always be ignored
It automatically lengthens the Montana term
It can be hidden if no Montana client asks
questions.explanation: The disciplinary section lists denial, refusal to renew and other commission limitations in another state.
feedback: Correct. The disciplinary section lists denial, refusal to renew and other commission limitations in another state.
The statute expressly makes that history relevant.
It does not extend a commission term.
Concealment can create additional application concerns.

questions.stem: After a Montana notary violates a notarial rule, the SOS requires an approved education class. Is that remedial measure supported?
options: No, education is allowed only for first applicants
No, a bond payment prohibits education requirements
Only the employer may require education
Yes, the statute permits required approved education after a violation
questions.explanation: The SOS may require approved notary education after a qualifying violation.
feedback: The provision includes current notaries with violations.
A bond payment does not remove the SOS's statutory authority.
The statute grants the authority to the SOS.
Correct. The SOS may require approved notary education after a qualifying violation.

questions.stem: A notary renews her Montana commission but closes her old journal. When is the old journal's ordinary retention measured from?
options: The day the empty journal was purchased
The first entry in the new journal
The last notarial act chronicled in that journal
The renewal fee payment
questions.explanation: The ordinary journal period is ten years after the last recorded act.
feedback: Purchase does not begin the final retention period.
A new journal's first entry does not set the old journal's deadline.
Correct. The ordinary journal period is ten years after the last recorded act.
Renewal payment is not the retention trigger.

questions.stem: A Montana notary resigns instead of renewing and keeps the records in authorized custody. What SOS notice does the section require?
options: Only a photograph of the discarded stamp
The journal's location
Every client's current bank balance
The employer's private payroll password
questions.explanation: A resigning notary must notify the SOS of the journal's location.
feedback: A stamp photograph does not identify the journal's location.
Correct. A resigning notary must notify the SOS of the journal's location.
The section does not require clients' bank balances.
A payroll password is unrelated and inappropriate.

questions.stem: A deceased Montana notary's personal representative finds the stamping device. What duty applies?
options: Render the device unusable
Use it to complete future client requests
Sell it as an active notary stamp
Give it to another notary for official use
questions.explanation: The personal representative or knowing possessor must disable the deceased notary's device.
feedback: Correct. The personal representative or knowing possessor must disable the deceased notary's device.
The representative does not inherit notarial authority.
It must not remain available for official use.
Another notary may not use that individual's device.

questions.stem: A bank notary has dealt personally with a customer over many years and is reasonably certain of his identity. Which Montana identity method may apply?
options: An anonymous internet recommendation
Automatic identity from the document's letterhead
Identity established only by the fee receipt
Personal knowledge
questions.explanation: Personal knowledge arises from dealings sufficient to provide reasonable certainty of identity.
feedback: An anonymous recommendation is not personal dealings.
Letterhead does not establish the present individual's identity.
A fee receipt is not the prescribed identification method.
Correct. Personal knowledge arises from dealings sufficient to provide reasonable certainty of identity.

questions.stem: An unfamiliar caller tells a Montana notary that everyone in town knows him. Has the caller thereby established the notary's personal knowledge?
options: Yes, if the caller provides a social-media username
Yes, because identity is the document drafter's duty
No, the notary needs qualifying personal dealings or satisfactory evidence
Yes, local popularity automatically suffices
questions.explanation: Personal knowledge belongs to the notary's sufficient dealings with the individual.
feedback: A username alone is not the statutory personal-knowledge test.
The notary must make the required identity determination.
Correct. Personal knowledge belongs to the notary's sufficient dealings with the individual.
Popularity does not establish the notary's personal knowledge.

questions.stem: At a Montana office, a signer presents a driver's license expired four years ago and no other identity basis. What prevents reliance on this credential under the listed allowance?
options: Only an employer-issued card is permitted
It exceeds the three-year expiration allowance
All driver's licenses are prohibited
The credential must show Montana birthplace
questions.explanation: The listed credential may not be expired more than three years before the act.
feedback: A private employer card is not the listed substitute.
Correct. The listed credential may not be expired more than three years before the act.
Driver's licenses are expressly listed.
Birthplace is not the stated expiration condition.

questions.stem: A nondriver asks whether Montana's identification list excludes a current government-issued nondriver credential. What is accurate?
options: That credential is expressly listed
A driver's license is the only accepted category
Nondrivers cannot obtain notarization
The signer must buy a private membership card
questions.explanation: The documentary list includes government-issued nondriver identification credentials.
feedback: Correct. The documentary list includes government-issued nondriver identification credentials.
The list includes other credential categories.
Driving status does not itself bar notarization.
Private membership does not replace statutory identification.

questions.stem: A signer offers another type of government ID with a photograph but no signature. Which issue should the Montana notary evaluate?
options: Whether every government ID must contain both signature and photograph
Whether an employer must approve the photograph
Whether a fee waiver removes identity review
Whether it meets timing requirements and is satisfactory to the notary
questions.explanation: The other-government-ID category requires a signature or photograph, acceptable timing and the notary's satisfaction.
feedback: The provision uses an alternative between signature and photograph.
Employer approval is not the statutory test.
Free acts still require identification.
Correct. The other-government-ID category requires a signature or photograph, acceptable timing and the notary's satisfaction.

questions.stem: A government-issued identification record is current and bears the individual's signature but no photograph. Under Montana's other-government-ID category, what is accurate?
options: A signature-only government record guarantees acceptance
The notary must copy its full number into the journal
The signature can satisfy the feature requirement if the credential is satisfactory
Every identification record needs a photograph regardless of category

questions.stem: A Montana customer asks for a stamp impression on a blank sheet with no completed notarial certificate. What restriction applies?

questions.explanation: The officer may select one or more systems and cannot be required to use an unselected system.
feedback: The law gives the officer a selection role.
Correct. The officer may select one or more systems and cannot be required to use an unselected system.
The statute limits that demand.
A purchase order is not state approval.

questions.stem: Before first using communication technology, a Montana notary plans to notify the SOS but conceal which technology will be used. Which requirement is missing?
options: Identify the intended system or technology
Provide only the client's nickname
Provide only an unrelated insurance quote
Wait to disclose technology until a lawsuit
questions.explanation: The pre-use notice must identify the intended electronic system or communication technology.
feedback: Correct. The pre-use notice must identify the intended electronic system or communication technology.
A nickname does not identify the technology.
An insurance quote is not the required identification.
The statute requires notice before initial use.

questions.stem: A commissioned Montana notary registers a system but has never taken the approved technology course or its exam. What additional prerequisite applies?
options: Only buy a faster computer
Only ask the first client to teach the system
Use another notary's certificate
Complete the approved instruction and pass its examination, with proof submitted
questions.explanation: Technology practice requires the approved course, course examination and completion proof.
feedback: Hardware does not replace the course.
Client instruction does not establish the required approval.
Another person's completion proof does not establish the notary's qualification.
Correct. Technology practice requires the approved course, course examination and completion proof.

questions.stem: A Montana notary has selected an electronic platform but does not know how to operate the feature required for this act. What is the mandatory response?

Assume selection alone guarantees competence
Refuse the request requiring unfamiliar operation
Proceed and experiment on the live act

feedback: The signer does not perform the officer's duties.
Selection does not eliminate the operation requirement.
Correct. The statute requires refusal when the requested system or technology is one the notary does not know how to operate.
Experimenting does not meet the required competency.

questions.stem: A Montana platform fails the state's applicable technology standards but offers a large discount. What should the notary do?

Refuse an act requiring that noncompliant technology
Accept because pricing determines compliance
Let the client waive the standards
questions.explanation: A request requiring technology that fails applicable standards must be refused.
feedback: Concealing the provider does not cure the defect.

questions.stem: A Montana remote notary travels to Idaho while the signer remains in Montana. Can the notary perform the Montana remote act from Idaho under this provision?

Yes, because the server is in Montana
Yes, if the notary keeps a Montana mailing address

feedback: Correct. Montana remote performance requires the officer's physical location in Montana at the act.
The signer's location does not satisfy the officer-location condition.
Server location does not supply the officer's location.
A mailing address does not establish physical presence.

questions.stem: A principal abroad requests Montana RON for a record concerning Montana land. Which international-connection condition can that subject satisfy?

An exemption from identification
An exemption from audiovisual recording
Property located in the territorial jurisdiction of the United States

feedback: The foreign-jurisdiction condition still must be checked.
The identity requirement remains.
The recording requirement remains.

questions.stem: A Montana officer knows the requested remote act is prohibited where the overseas principal is physically located. What does the cross-border condition require?

Do not perform the act under that known prohibition
Ignore foreign prohibitions whenever the fee is prepaid

feedback: Hiding a location does not remove the prohibition.
File-storage location does not remove this condition.
Correct. The international route requires that the officer not know the act is prohibited in the principal's jurisdiction.
Prepayment does not waive the condition.

questions.stem: An overseas principal needs a document for a matter before a United States court. Which nexus provision should a Montana remote officer check?

A matter filed with or before a United States-located public official, court or entity
Only the principal's foreign citizenship
Only the language of the computer menu
questions.explanation: The listed matter-before-an-entity connection is one recognized United States nexus.
feedback: Payment-card origin does not establish the record's connection.
Correct. The listed matter-before-an-entity connection is one recognized United States nexus.
Citizenship alone is not the specified record nexus.
Menu language does not establish it.

questions.stem: A Montana remote notary proposes splitting one notarization across separate unrecorded phone calls. What session condition is missing?
options: Execution in a single recorded session complying with the law
A requirement to use ordinary telephone audio only
A rule allowing any number of undocumented sessions
An exemption whenever the participants know one another
questions.explanation: The remote act must be executed in a single recorded compliant session.
feedback: Correct. The remote act must be executed in a single recorded compliant session.
Audio-only calls do not supply the prescribed audiovisual procedure.
The statute sets a single-recorded-session condition.
Familiarity does not remove the session requirement.

questions.stem: In a Montana remote session, the signer displays one record while the notary has a materially different version. What must be resolved?

Only whether both documents have blank margins
Only whether the vendor accepts payment
That both are using the same record presented for notarization

feedback: A filename does not resolve substantive record identity.
Margins do not establish matching content.
Payment does not establish record identity.
Correct. The officer must be satisfied the remotely notarized record is the same record presented by the principal.

A requirement to print every screen
Sufficient communication quality
A requirement for the most expensive internet package

feedback: One device brand is not the stated requirement.
Printing screens does not cure inadequate live communication.
Correct. The officer must be satisfied the technology quality permits the required legal determinations.
The statute focuses on sufficiency rather than a particular price.

questions.stem: A Montana remote system allows anyone with a public link to enter the signing session without authentication. Which safeguard should be addressed?

Removal of all identity checks

feedback: Publishing a password undermines secure authentication.
Correct. The officer must take reasonable steps for reasonably secure authenticated access.
Charging more does not secure access.
Removing checks worsens the missing safeguard.

questions.stem: A Montana remote workflow lets a required witness see a different document and adds attachments after the live session. Which safeguards are implicated?
options: Shared record viewing and real-time signatures, changes and attachments
Only the notary's annual filing fee
Only the printer's ink color
Only the client's preferred filename
questions.explanation: The participants must view the same record and the listed record actions occur in real time.
feedback: Correct. The participants must view the same record and the listed record actions occur in real time.
An annual fee does not address session integrity.
Printer ink does not establish electronic session compliance.
Filename preference does not resolve the required safeguards.

questions.stem: A principal in Florida completes a compliant remote act with an officer physically in Montana. Which law governs the notarial act under this provision?
options: Whichever law the vendor prefers
Only the principal's preferred law
No state's law because the act is online
Montana law

feedback: Vendor preference does not determine the statutory rule.
The principal's preference does not replace it.
Online performance does not remove governing law.
Correct. A communication-technology act under the provision is deemed performed in Montana and governed by Montana law.

questions.stem: A Montana remote signer signs a paper document that is then delivered to the notary. Which act does the SOS say can use its remote-paper method?
options: Every remote signature witnessing on any paper
Any act without appearance
An acknowledgment
Every jurat automatically

feedback: It does not broadly authorize paper signature witnessing by this method.
The method still requires compliant appearance.
Correct. The SOS describes acknowledgments as the only acts performed through that remote-paper method.
The published remote-paper description does not include every jurat.

questions.stem: A client calls a Montana paper-and-wet-signature remote acknowledgment RON. What record distinction should the officer recognize?
options: The distinction depends solely on the client's age
RON uses an electronic record, while the described remote-paper method uses a tangible record
All video calls necessarily create electronic records
The distinction depends solely on the fee
questions.explanation: Montana distinguishes its electronic-record RON method from the separate tangible-record remote method.
feedback: Client age does not determine the method.
Correct. Montana distinguishes its electronic-record RON method from the separate tangible-record remote method.
A video connection does not transform paper into an electronic record.
The record and procedure determine the method.

questions.stem: A Montana remote notary stops using a vendor and wants a repository to hold preserved recordings. Which repository condition applies?
options: Approval by the SOS
Any anonymous file-sharing account
Only the lowest annual price
No condition if the vendor is leaving the market
questions.explanation: The statutory transfer alternative uses a repository approved by the SOS.
feedback: Correct. The statutory transfer alternative uses a repository approved by the SOS.
An anonymous account does not establish approval.
Price alone does not establish statutory approval.
A vendor's exit does not remove the repository condition.

questions.stem: An electronic-system provider tells a Montana notary it has no responsibility to take steps addressing the notary's ability to use the system lawfully. What does the section state?
options: Only clients must train the officer
Every vendor disclaimer overrides the statute
Technology knowledge is optional
The provider must take reasonable steps to ensure the notary has the required knowledge
questions.explanation: The provider has the reasonable-steps knowledge obligation stated in subsection (2).
feedback: The statute assigns a provider responsibility.
A disclaimer does not erase the statutory obligation.
Lawful system knowledge is not optional under this provision.
Correct. The provider has the reasonable-steps knowledge obligation stated in subsection (2).

questions.stem: A Montana electronic system stores the notary's seal separately so it cannot be copied with the notarized electronic record. What capability is required?
options: Only storing the vendor's logo
Only showing the seal before signing
Copying the seal together with the associated record
Only displaying a temporary advertisement
questions.explanation: The electronic official stamp must be capable of being copied together with the associated record.
feedback: The vendor logo is not the notary's seal.
A temporary display does not supply the required enduring association.
Correct. The electronic official stamp must be capable of being copied together with the associated record.
An advertisement is not the official-stamp capability.

questions.stem: After an electronic Montana act, a missing official stamp image is discovered. What correction pathway does the section provide?
options: Erase the journal record
Attach or logically associate the missing image and document the correction as required
Replace the underlying transaction with a different deal
Let any unrelated notary silently change the file
questions.explanation: The section permits supplying a missing electronic stamp image subject to its correction controls.
feedback: The journal record supports rather than disappears from the repair.
Correct. The section permits supplying a missing electronic stamp image subject to its correction controls.
The correction provision does not authorize a different transaction.
Correction authority and documentation remain limited.

questions.stem: A Montana office still uses an old checklist demanding notarization of every individual-to-individual title transfer. What update should the officer consult?
options: The SOS notice explaining removal of the former requirement effective October 1, 2025
A claim that an old checklist overrides all later law
A private printer's advertisement
An assumption that removal began only after every old form disappeared
questions.explanation: The SOS identifies the statutory change and its October 1, 2025 effective date.
feedback: Correct. The SOS identifies the statutory change and its October 1, 2025 effective date.
A stale checklist does not override the amendment.
Advertising is not the authoritative update.
The effective date does not depend on depletion of old forms.

questions.stem: A Montana seller thinks the notarization change means a paper title can be handed over completely unassigned. Which remaining transfer duty does the statute describe?
options: Every seller may omit the transfer assignment
A stamp impression alone transfers ownership
The seller may always keep the assigned title indefinitely
Execute the transfer in the appropriate title space and deliver the assigned title as prescribed
questions.explanation: The current statute retains the owner's assignment and delivery duties.
feedback: Removing the former notary requirement does not erase the assignment duty.
A stamp alone does not execute the owner's title transfer.
The section specifies delivery routes.
Correct. The current statute retains the owner's assignment and delivery duties.

questions.stem: A Montana transfer uses an electronic title record. Which written-authorization route does the current section describe for the owner?
options: Let the notary invent the owner's authorization
Assume electronic records require no owner action
Authorize the specified agent or county treasurer on the prescribed form to enter the transfer
Send any unsigned social-media message

feedback: The officer cannot invent the owner's consent.
The statute retains owner authorization duties.
Correct. The electronic route uses the owner's written authorization on the prescribed form.
An unsigned message is not the described prescribed authorization.

questions.stem: A Montana buyer says receiving an assigned title eliminates every title-application step. What does the section ordinarily require of the transferee?
options: Wait until the next resale before any application
Execute the prescribed title application
Obtain only the notary's business card
Replace the title with a personal diary entry
questions.explanation: Subject to the section's stated exception, the transferee must execute a title application in the prescribed form.
feedback: The statute imposes duties following this transfer.
Correct. Subject to the section's stated exception, the transferee must execute a title application in the prescribed form.
A business card is not the application.
A diary entry does not replace the prescribed filing.

questions.stem: A Montana buyer assumes the former title-notarization repeal creates unlimited time to handle the title and registration obligations. Which stated period should be checked?
options: The section's 40-day period after transfer
A universal lifetime extension
Only the seller's next commission expiration
Only the notary's next renewal date
questions.explanation: The current section describes the transferee's specified duties within 40 days after transfer.
feedback: Correct. The current section describes the transferee's specified duties within 40 days after transfer.
The section imposes a time period.
The seller's commission does not determine vehicle filing timing.
A notary's renewal date is unrelated.

questions.stem: A transferee fails to comply with Montana's specified requirements within the 40-day vehicle-transfer grace period. What late penalty does this subsection state?

An unlimited notarial-act surcharge
Automatic forgiveness after buying a stamp
A $10 late penalty

feedback: The vehicle penalty does not automatically cancel notary commissions.

Buying notary supplies does not waive the penalty.

questions.stem: A Montana customer asks a private notary to copy-certify an official vehicle title. The notary is not employed by the issuing or original-holding public entity. Which boundary remains despite the transfer change?
options: An exception created by owning a vehicle
An exception created by waiving the notarial fee
The official-record copy-certification restriction
Automatic authority to certify every government record
questions.explanation: The separate official-record restriction still applies to the notary's copy-certification authority.
feedback: Vehicle ownership is not the statutory employment exception.
A fee waiver does not create the exception.
Correct. The separate official-record restriction still applies to the notary's copy-certification authority.
The transfer amendment does not confer blanket public-record certification authority.

questions.stem: A Montana buyer asks whether the removal of the former title notarization requirement guarantees that every other transfer document is complete. What distinction is accurate?
options: Every transaction involving a vehicle is exempt from all paperwork
The current transfer and application duties still must be checked separately
The amendment certifies every sales contract's legal sufficiency
A notary stamp guarantees registration approval
questions.explanation: The current section retains substantive owner and transferee duties after the former notarization requirement was removed.
feedback: The current law still specifies paperwork and filing duties.
Correct. The current section retains substantive owner and transferee duties after the former notarization requirement was removed.
