cards.title: Eligibility belongs to the individual
cards.front: What must an applicant establish before holding a Montana commission?
cards.rule: Meet the age, United States status, English literacy and qualifying Montana-connection requirements, along with education, examination and integrity conditions.
cards.boundary: A qualifying nonresident connection may satisfy the geographical requirement.
cards.mixup: An employer's desire for a notary does not establish the applicant's qualifications.

cards.title: Qualifying Montana connections
cards.front: Which connections can support a nonresident application?
cards.rule: The section lists qualifying military-family status, a registered and appropriately licensed Montana business, regular qualifying employment, or current Montana professional licensure.
cards.boundary: Each alternative has its own factual conditions.
cards.mixup: Occasional visits alone do not establish a listed connection.

cards.title: Assurance stays active
cards.front: Why should a commissioned notary track assurance cancellation?
cards.rule: A valid $25,000 assurance must remain on file for acts performed in Montana.
cards.boundary: The assurance must use an authorized issuer and prescribed form.
cards.mixup: The expiration printed on the commission does not resolve a canceled assurance.

cards.title: Candor in commissioning
cards.front: What can an application omission jeopardize?
cards.rule: A fraudulent, dishonest or deceitful application omission may support denial, refusal to renew or other commission action.
cards.boundary: Other specified grounds can also affect commissioning.
cards.mixup: Paying the filing fee does not guarantee approval.

cards.title: Mandatory refusal
cards.front: Which uncertainties require refusing an act?
cards.rule: Refuse when unsatisfied about the individual's competence or capacity, or knowing or voluntary execution.
cards.boundary: Refusal may also be required for unfamiliar or noncompliant technology.
cards.mixup: A relative's reassurance does not replace the officer's determination.

cards.title: Education and examination
cards.front: What are the two learning prerequisites for a first commission?
cards.rule: Complete at least four approved education hours within the previous 12 months and pass the required examination.
cards.boundary: Approved authorities include the SOS and the commission of continuing legal education for the stated education requirement.
cards.mixup: An examination pass alone does not award the required course hours.

cards.title: Exam recency
cards.front: How recent must a Montana passing result be when applying?
cards.rule: The SOS requires the examination pass no more than six months before submission.
cards.boundary: Retain the examination certificate for the filing.
cards.mixup: A four-year commission term does not mean a score remains current for four years.

cards.title: Attempt limits
cards.front: What does the SOS specify after three failed attempts?
cards.rule: The passing grade is 80%. After three unsuccessful attempts, wait three months before another examination attempt.
cards.boundary: Use the official gateway and current instructions.
cards.mixup: A private website's practice percentage does not itself establish an official pass.

cards.title: The curriculum's scope
cards.front: What subjects belong in Montana examination preparation?
cards.rule: Study the laws, rules, procedures and ethics relevant to notarial acts.
cards.boundary: The examination is based on the statutorily described course.
cards.mixup: Retail supply choices cover only a small part of practical preparation.

cards.title: Completion evidence
cards.front: What should remain available after the courses and examination?
cards.rule: Keep usable training and examination completion certificates for upload with the bond and other required application documents.
cards.boundary: A purchase receipt may show payment without proving successful completion.
cards.mixup: Deleting the certificate after viewing a pass can delay filing.
cards.source: SOS online application steps — required documents

cards.title: Personal knowledge
cards.front: How does Montana define a personal-knowledge basis?
cards.rule: The officer knows the individual through dealings sufficient to provide reasonable certainty of the claimed identity.
cards.boundary: Evaluate the officer's actual dealings with that person.
cards.mixup: A claim of local popularity does not establish the officer's personal knowledge.

cards.title: Credential timing
cards.front: Which listed credentials have an expiration allowance?
cards.rule: A passport, driver's license or government nondriver credential may be current or expired no more than three years before the act.
cards.boundary: Other government identification has additional feature and satisfaction conditions.
cards.mixup: A card's official appearance does not remove timing or identity concerns.

cards.title: Credible witnesses
cards.front: What gives credible-witness identification its formal character?
cards.rule: The identification is supplied by the witness's oath or affirmation, with the witness appearing and identified under the applicable provision.
cards.boundary: Physical and technology appearances have different identification details.
cards.mixup: An unsworn text message does not perform the witness procedure.

cards.title: Representative execution
cards.front: What must be checked when someone signs for an entity?
cards.rule: Determine the individual's identity and establish the claimed title or capacity and knowing, willing execution in that capacity through the permitted evidence.
cards.boundary: The officer may refuse when the capacity evidence is unsatisfactory.
cards.mixup: An impressive company logo does not identify the individual representative.

cards.title: Additional evidence
cards.front: What can an officer request when identity remains uncertain?
cards.rule: Require additional information or credentials necessary to assure the individual's identity.
cards.boundary: The listed documentary category does not require accepting evidence that leaves the officer unassured.
cards.mixup: Client urgency does not replace the statutory determination.

cards.title: One act, a timely record
cards.front: When does journal work belong in the transaction?
cards.rule: Make the entry contemporaneously and record the date, time, record description and act type, principal information, identity method and any fee.
cards.boundary: Technology and signature exceptions add specific details.
cards.mixup: A week-end reconstruction from memory misses the contemporaneous requirement.

cards.title: Sensitive data exclusions
cards.front: Which identity details must stay out of the journal?
cards.rule: Do not record a Social Security number, passport number, driver's license number or birth date.
cards.boundary: Record the permitted credential description and issuance or expiration date instead.
cards.mixup: Client consent does not create a statutory exception to the exclusion.

cards.title: Original journal control
cards.front: How does a departing employee protect the original journal?
cards.rule: Keep sole control and do not surrender it to the employer on termination without SOS approval.
cards.boundary: The employer may retain a copy of employment-scope acts.
cards.mixup: Paying for the journal does not automatically entitle the employer to the original.

cards.title: Public access conditions
cards.front: What makes an ordinary journal-entry request sufficiently specific?
cards.rule: A signed tangible or electronic request identifies the month, year, record type and principal. Access is limited to the specified entry while the notary retains control.
cards.boundary: The notary must be satisfied the request has no criminal or other illegal purpose.
cards.mixup: A request for one entry does not authorize taking the whole journal.

cards.title: Two retention clocks
cards.front: How do ordinary journal and audiovisual retention triggers differ?
cards.rule: Retain the journal ten years after its last chronicled act. Retain a recording ten years from its recording date, subject to the authorized repository alternatives.
cards.boundary: Revocation, death and incompetency trigger specific transfer duties.
cards.mixup: Renewal does not erase either records obligation.

cards.title: The signature on file
cards.front: What links everyday certificate signing to the commission record?
cards.rule: The official signature is filed with the SOS and later official signatures must be reasonably similar.
cards.boundary: Tangible official signatures use blue or black ink.
cards.mixup: A client cannot choose an unrelated signature for the notary.

cards.title: Electronic stamp consistency
cards.front: Which tangible-stamp characteristics carry into the electronic image?
cards.rule: Match the format, color, content and approximate size, with the required capability of being copied together with the associated record.
cards.boundary: The electronic image still needs proper association with the notarized record.
cards.mixup: A vendor's logo does not replace the notary's official stamp.

cards.title: Device control
cards.front: Who may use the stamping device?
cards.rule: The notary is its sole owner, responsible for security, and must not let another individual use it for a notarial act or another reason.
cards.boundary: Promptly notify the SOS if it is lost, stolen or inaccessible.
cards.mixup: Employer payment does not authorize coworker use.

cards.title: Act fees and extras
cards.front: What should a mobile-service quote distinguish?
cards.rule: The listed notarial-act fee is capped at $10 per act. Additional travel or technology fees require the statutory explanation and advance agreement.
cards.boundary: Travel charges also have the IRS standard-mileage ceiling.
cards.mixup: Agreement to an extra charge does not remove the specific statutory travel limit.

cards.title: Retiring a device
cards.front: When must a stamping device become unusable?
cards.rule: Disable it on resignation, revocation, commission expiration or expiration of its displayed date. The death or incompetency provision places a related duty on the specified possessor.
cards.boundary: Disabling can use a method that renders the device unusable.
cards.mixup: Keeping a working old-date stamp available invites unauthorized use.

cards.title: The execution inquiry
cards.front: What does a Montana acknowledgment establish about a signature?
cards.rule: Determine the appearing individual's identity and that the signature is that individual's knowing and willing execution for the intended purposes.
cards.boundary: Representative records add a capacity determination.
cards.mixup: Identifying the person does not resolve a disputed or involuntary signature.

cards.title: Certificate essentials
cards.front: Which transaction facts belong in the certificate?
cards.rule: Identify the act, venue and principal or other required subject, and include the officer's signature, date, title and official stamp.
cards.boundary: Execute the certificate contemporaneously.
cards.mixup: A stamp by itself does not describe the notarial act.

cards.title: A certificate stays attached
cards.front: How should a certificate connect to the record?
cards.rule: A tangible certificate is part of or securely affixed to the record. An electronic certificate is attached or logically associated.
cards.boundary: Remote certificates additionally disclose communication technology.
cards.mixup: A loose reusable certificate does not preserve the required record connection.

cards.title: Evidence-based corrections
cards.front: What supports a later certificate repair?
cards.rule: The original officer may make or authorize a correction supported by the journal, date and initial it, and note the change in the journal.
cards.boundary: A third-party change needs written authorization and the required retained copies.
cards.mixup: The statute permits a subsequent proper stamp image while forbidding editing the existing impression.

cards.title: Signer and officer conflicts
cards.front: Which personal roles can disqualify the notary?
cards.rule: Self-signature notarization, an individually named record, direct transactional benefit, and the specified corporate representative-signing situation are prohibited.
cards.boundary: Evaluate the notary's actual role in the particular record.
cards.mixup: A different client's signature on the same record does not automatically eliminate the notary's disqualification.

cards.title: A solemn participant's act
cards.front: What makes an oath or affirmation more than a signature?
cards.rule: The person knowingly and willingly makes the statement with intent to be bound, and the officer establishes the person's identity.
cards.boundary: The person must participate through the authorized appearance method.
cards.mixup: A silent stamp does not administer a solemn declaration.

cards.title: Verification requirements
cards.front: What must the officer determine for a verification on oath or affirmation?
cards.rule: Identify the appearing person who signs and makes the verification and determine that the signature was made knowingly and willingly for the intended purposes.
cards.boundary: Use the proper oath-or-affirmation procedure.
cards.mixup: A genuine-looking signature alone does not complete the verification.

cards.title: Deposition transcript boundaries
cards.front: What governs certification connected with a deposition oath?
cards.rule: Certify the matters required by the notarial law, other applicable laws or the court of jurisdiction.
cards.boundary: The deposition-transcript journal-signature exception does not erase the rest of the journal entry.
cards.mixup: A typist's preferred certificate cannot override governing requirements.

cards.title: Directed alternate signing
cards.front: How can a physically unable principal execute a record?
cards.rule: The principal may direct someone other than the notarial officer to sign. Add the explanatory direction notation and record both persons' names and addresses.
cards.boundary: The principal remains the person intending to execute the record.
cards.mixup: A helper's signature does not make the directing principal disappear from the procedure.

cards.title: Legal-service boundaries
cards.front: What professional services does the commission leave unauthorized?
cards.rule: The commission does not authorize drafting legal records, legal advice, immigration consulting or immigration representation, or compensation for those activities.
cards.boundary: A separate professional authorization must supply any lawful legal-service authority.
cards.mixup: Administering an oath does not confer an attorney's powers.

cards.title: Choose the exact method
cards.front: How do IPEN, RON and Montana remote paper acts differ?
cards.rule: IPEN keeps physical appearance with an electronic record. RON uses communication technology and an electronic record. The described remote-paper method uses tangible records for acknowledgments.
cards.boundary: For these technology methods the officer must be in Montana.
cards.mixup: A video connection alone does not identify the legal method.

cards.title: Pre-use qualifications
cards.front: What precedes a notary's first technology-based act?
cards.rule: Select the system, notify the SOS and identify it, then satisfy approved technology instruction, examination and proof-submission requirements.
cards.boundary: The officer cannot be forced to use an unselected electronic system.
cards.mixup: Buying a subscription does not establish qualification.

cards.title: Same record in real time
cards.front: Which integrity safeguards matter during a remote session?
cards.rule: Confirm the record's identity, have the principal and required witness view the same record, and ensure signatures, changes and attachments occur in real time.
cards.boundary: Secure authentication and sufficient communication quality also apply.
cards.mixup: Matching filenames alone cannot establish matching records.

cards.title: Overseas principal
cards.front: What must be checked for an international remote request?
cards.rule: The act must not be known to be prohibited where the principal is located, and the record needs the specified United States matter, property or transaction connection.
cards.boundary: The notary stays physically in Montana.
cards.mixup: United States file storage alone does not establish the transaction nexus.

cards.title: Session evidence
cards.front: What records accompany compliant communication-technology work?
cards.rule: Record the entire communication and make the required journal entry, including the recording's storage location and technology details.
cards.boundary: The certificate identifies the technology appearance.
cards.mixup: An audiovisual recording does not replace the separate journal.

cards.title: Read the effective update
cards.front: What changed in Montana individual-to-individual title transfers?
cards.rule: The SOS states that the former transferor-signature acknowledgment requirement was removed effective October 1, 2025.
cards.boundary: Check current agency instructions for the actual transaction.
cards.mixup: A remaining blank stamp box on an old form does not itself prove a current requirement.

cards.title: Owner assignment duties
cards.front: What must an owner still do when voluntarily transferring a titled vehicle?
cards.rule: Use the prescribed electronic authorization route or execute and deliver the assigned tangible title through the section's specified route.
cards.boundary: The current statute retains owner transfer duties.
cards.mixup: Removal of the former acknowledgment requirement does not turn an unassigned title into a completed transfer.

cards.title: Transferee filing duties
cards.front: What timing should the transferee check after transfer?
cards.rule: The section states the transferee's title-application and registration routes within 40 days, subject to its specified exception and cross-references.
cards.boundary: A $10 late penalty applies under the stated noncompliance provision.
cards.mixup: The notary's commission renewal date does not control vehicle filing time.

cards.title: Public-record copy limits
cards.front: How does a vehicle-title request interact with copy-certification restrictions?
cards.rule: Official-record copy certification remains subject to the exception for employment by the public entity issuing or holding the original record.
cards.boundary: Distinguish the requested copy act from an owner's transfer assignment.
cards.mixup: The vehicle-transfer change does not create blanket authority to certify government records.

cards.title: Route administrative questions
cards.front: Where should detailed Montana title-transfer questions go?
cards.rule: The SOS directs additional vehicle-transfer questions to the Title and Registration Bureau.
cards.boundary: Use the current statutory duties and agency instructions for the transfer involved.
cards.mixup: A notary commission does not guarantee the agency will approve a client's transfer paperwork.
cards.source: SOS Vehicle Title Transfer Updates — agency referral

cards.title: Two education routes
cards.front: How can an applicant satisfy Montana renewal education?
cards.rule: Use at least four approved continuing hours in the previous 12 months or at least two approved hours in each of the preceding three years.
cards.boundary: A six-hour total does not establish the each-year alternative without the yearly distribution.
cards.mixup: Check the recent-four-hour route separately when hours are concentrated.

cards.title: Renewal retains the exam
cards.front: Which prior achievement does renewal still require?
cards.rule: An applicant for a renewed commission must pass the required examination and provide completion evidence.
cards.boundary: The SOS applies its examination-recency and attempt instructions to renewing applicants.
cards.mixup: A pass from the previous commission term does not automatically establish current recency.

cards.title: The portal window
cards.front: What is the published Montana renewal submission window?
cards.rule: The online system permits filing during the 30 days before expiration and the 30-day grace period afterward.
cards.boundary: An expired commission does not supply current authority during the grace interval.
cards.mixup: A filing window is different from an extension of the commission.

cards.title: Renewal and old records
cards.front: What happens to a journal when a commission renews?
cards.rule: Continue preserving it for the required period measured from the last act chronicled, including after closing the book.
cards.boundary: Specific transfer rules apply on revocation, death or incompetency.
cards.mixup: A new commission does not authorize disposal of the old journal.

cards.title: A current assurance for the term
cards.front: What must accompany the renewed commission's valid operation?
cards.rule: The prescribed assurance must cover acts during the commission term and remain valid on file.
cards.boundary: Issuer cancellation and claim-payment notices have their own statutory deadlines.
cards.mixup: An old insurance receipt does not prove a current assurance is on file.

application.summary: Establish individual eligibility, complete the required filing evidence and maintain authority throughout commissioned work.

sections.heading: Choose the actual eligibility route
sections.body: MCA 1-5-619 requires age 18, United States citizenship or permanent legal residency, English literacy and one qualifying Montana connection. A nonresident should identify the precise employment, business, professional-license or military-family alternative relied on and verify its conditions. Approval also depends on the learning requirements and the integrity grounds in 1-5-621.

sections.heading: Separate filing from authority
sections.body: The application requires its fee, oath, assurance and completion certification. The $25,000 assurance must come from a licensed or authorized issuer, use the prescribed form and cover acts during the term. Under 1-5-619(4)(d), a valid assurance must remain on file. A pending application does not create a new commission or extend an expired one.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A small professional office has staff working both in Montana and Idaho. Its owner wants one employee commissioned. The employee identifies regular employment at the appropriately registered and licensed Montana office as the connection route, checks the other personal qualifications and completes the individual application. Buying office supplies for that employee does not itself appoint the person.

keyFacts: One individual cannot hold concurrent effective Montana notary commissions.
The statutory term is four years.
Valid assurance on file is a continuing condition.

examination.summary: Treat approved education, a current examination pass and retained completion evidence as separate parts of qualification.

sections.heading: Plan both learning requirements
sections.body: MCA 1-5-620 bases the examination on a course covering notarial laws, rules, procedures and ethics. For an initial commission, at least four approved hours must fall within the preceding 12 months. A course vendor's sale receipt does not necessarily demonstrate completion, approval or an examination pass.

sections.heading: Use the official examination instructions
sections.body: The SOS application page applies an 80% passing grade, requires the pass no more than six months before application and imposes a three-month wait after three failures. Save the issued examination certificate and the education certificates for the online filing. The practice site's session length does not establish an official question count or time limit.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A learner schedules the course early, then delays applying while changing jobs. Before filing, the learner checks the dates of both course completion and the examination pass independently. If one falls outside its applicable window, a recent date on the other certificate does not repair the old prerequisite.

keyFacts: Initial approved education must be within the previous 12 months.
The SOS states an 80% passing grade.
The official score-recency instruction is six months before application.

identity.summary: Identify the individual and evaluate any representative role through the evidence appropriate to the act and appearance method.

sections.heading: Build a defensible identity basis
sections.body: MCA 1-5-603(12) recognizes personal knowledge based on sufficient dealings, listed government credentials and the credible-witness procedure. The listed passport, driver's-license and nondriver credentials have a maximum three-year expiration allowance. Other government ID must also have the prescribed signature-or-photograph feature and satisfy the officer.

sections.heading: Distinguish a person from a capacity
sections.body: For representative acknowledgments and signature witnessings, 1-5-603(4) adds a title-or-capacity determination using the record, personal knowledge or an official record. The officer may refuse when the capacity evidence is unsatisfactory. Section (14) permits requesting additional identity information or credentials when necessary for assurance.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: An association's volunteer treasurer brings a contract and a current identification credential. The notary first evaluates the appearing individual's identity, then the treasurer's claimed capacity using the permitted evidence. A recognizable association letterhead alone does not answer both questions.

keyFacts: Personal knowledge requires sufficient dealings with the individual.
A credible witness supplies an oath or affirmation.
Identity and representative capacity are separate determinations.

journal-privacy.summary: Create a contemporaneous record while protecting excluded identity data and retaining lawful control of journals and recordings.

sections.heading: Record the transaction without excess identity data
sections.body: MCA 1-5-618(3) requires the act's date and time, record description, principal details, identity basis and fee, with additional technology details where applicable. Subsection (4) excludes Social Security, passport and driver's-license numbers and birth dates. Record the permitted credential description and issuance or expiration information instead.

sections.heading: Match access and retention to the record
sections.body: An ordinary journal request needs a signed, specific request, limited-entry disclosure and continued notary control, subject to the statute's official-access categories. A recording request has its separate reasonable-purpose condition. Ordinary journal retention runs ten years after the last chronicled act, while audiovisual retention runs ten years from the recording date, with authorized transfer provisions.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: After a regional office closes, the former employer requests its employment-related entries. The notary evaluates the copy permission in 1-5-618(5)(b), preserves the original under the applicable control rule and separates unrelated personal entries from the employer's request. Closing the office does not end the retention obligation.

keyFacts: All notarial acts belong in the required journal.
A recording supplements the technology act's journal entry.
Revocation, death and incompetency have specific repository-transfer rules.

stamp-security.summary: Maintain the filed official signature, compliant stamp images, secure devices and properly separated fee categories.

sections.heading: Protect the officer's means of authentication
sections.body: MCA 1-5-616 ties the official signature to the filed version and specifies blue or black ink on tangible records. The stamp includes the prescribed name, title, city and expiration information. Under 1-5-617 the notary owns and secures the device, prevents another person's use and promptly reports loss, theft or inaccessibility.

sections.heading: Price the actual service
sections.body: MCA 1-5-626 permits up to $10 for each listed act. Additional technology or travel charges require explanation and advance agreement under the statute. Travel has the additional IRS standard-mileage ceiling. A completed certificate's bad stamp is addressed through the correction provision in 1-5-609(5), which permits a subsequent proper impression and requires documentation.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A mobile notary prepares a written quote showing the actual acknowledgment service and the separately proposed travel charge. The notary explains the extra fee, checks the statutory mileage limit and obtains agreement before travel. A client accepting the quote does not make a noncompliant stamp or an excessive charge proper.

keyFacts: The official signature on tangible records uses blue or black ink.
Another individual may not use the notary's stamping device.
Act-fee limits and additional-fee conditions apply separately.

acknowledgment.summary: Determine knowing and willing execution, complete the certificate accurately and preserve the connection between certificate and record.

sections.heading: Document the act that occurred
sections.body: MCA 1-5-603(1) requires the appearing individual's identity and knowing, willing execution of that individual's signature for the intended purposes. The certificate requirements in 1-5-609 include act, venue, subject, signature, date, official title and stamp. Venue under 1-5-629 is the officer's physical state and county at the act.

sections.heading: Repair through evidence and retained authority
sections.body: A later correction must be supported by the transaction's journal record. Under 1-5-609(5), only the original notary may make or authorize the change, with dating, initials and a journal notation. A third-party repair needs written authorization and the prescribed retained copies. Existing stamp impressions cannot be edited, although a subsequent proper image is permitted.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A recording office returns a contract certificate with an omitted transaction detail. The original notary consults the journal to determine whether the requested detail is supportable, documents any authorized repair and keeps the required evidence. The client cannot simply choose a convenient replacement fact.

keyFacts: A tangible certificate must be part of or securely affixed to the record.
An electronic certificate must be attached or logically associated.
Correction authority stays with the officer who performed the notarization.

oath.summary: Use an actual oath or affirmation, the proper identity procedure and the execution accommodations recognized by Montana law.

sections.heading: Obtain a meaningful declaration
sections.body: MCA 1-5-603(2) and (7) require the identified participant's knowing and willing statement with intent to be bound. A verification involves the appearing person signing and making the verification. A certificate or silent stamp cannot supply the participant's missing solemn declaration. The officer must also apply the mandatory refusal rule when the required capacity or voluntariness is unresolved.

sections.heading: Accommodate execution without changing roles
sections.body: MCA 1-5-623 lets a physically unable principal direct another individual, other than the officer, to sign. The officer adds the prescribed explanatory notation and records both individuals' names and addresses. Deposition-related certification under 1-5-603(8) must satisfy the notarial law, other applicable laws or the court of jurisdiction.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A hospital patient understands the affidavit and can communicate an intent to affirm, but cannot physically write. The notary evaluates the identity and solemn declaration, then uses the directed-signature procedure with an eligible helper and its notation and journal details. Physical inability to write does not by itself appoint the notary as the alternate signer.

keyFacts: A signature alone does not administer an oath.
The directed signer must be someone other than the notarial officer.
A deposition-transcript signature exception does not eliminate the other journal details.

technology.summary: Select the precise Montana technology method and satisfy qualification, session-integrity and record-preservation requirements.

sections.heading: Choose and qualify for the method
sections.body: The SOS distinguishes physical-presence IPEN, electronic-record RON and its tangible-record remote acknowledgment method. MCA 1-5-615 requires selected systems, SOS notification and identification of the technology, approved instruction, the associated examination and proof. Section 1-5-622 requires refusal for unfamiliar or noncompliant technology.

sections.heading: Control the remote session
sections.body: MCA 1-5-603(10) requires the officer in Montana, a single recorded session, satisfactory identity, sufficient communication quality and assurance about the record's identity. Secure authentication, shared record viewing and real-time record changes also apply. Overseas principals need the stated United States nexus and foreign-jurisdiction condition. Preserve the entire communication and the separate journal under 1-5-618.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A signer abroad sends two similar versions of an electronic agreement before a session. The Montana officer identifies which record everyone will view and use, checks the overseas connection and then applies the session safeguards. Successful login alone does not settle which version is being notarized.

keyFacts: The remote officer must be physically in Montana.
The remote certificate discloses communication technology.
The recording and journal have distinct preservation requirements.

vehicle-titles.summary: Use the current Montana title-transfer rule and distinguish agency transfer duties from a separate requested notarial act.

sections.heading: Apply the 2025 change accurately
sections.body: The SOS states that the former transferor-signature acknowledgment requirement for individual-to-individual title transfers was removed effective October 1, 2025. Read that update alongside current MCA 61-3-220. The owner still uses the specified electronic authorization or tangible assignment-and-delivery route, and the transferee still has the section's application and registration duties.

sections.heading: Keep the service boundary clear
sections.body: The title-transfer change does not grant a private notary blanket copy-certification authority over official records. MCA 1-5-625(1)(c) retains its official-record employment exception. Questions about the particular transfer's agency paperwork belong with the Title and Registration Bureau or the appropriate filing office. A notarial commission does not itself guarantee title approval.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A family brings an old printed title checklist and a current agency form to a community counter. The notary identifies the effective SOS update, distinguishes the owner's assignment from the buyer's filing duties and refers transaction-specific agency questions appropriately. If a separate notarial service is requested, its own legal conditions still require evaluation.

keyFacts: The SOS gives October 1, 2025 as the change's effective date.
Current owner and transferee duties remain in MCA 61-3-220.
The title-transfer update does not erase official-record copy restrictions.

renewal.summary: Use the correct renewal education route, current examination evidence and term-specific assurance while preserving prior records.

sections.heading: Check education by its actual timing
sections.body: MCA 1-5-620 offers a recent-four-hour continuing-education route or at least two hours in each of the preceding three years. Keep certificates that show approval and dates. The three-year alternative cannot be established from a six-hour total that gives no year-by-year distribution. Renewing applicants also need the required examination pass.

sections.heading: Manage the transition between terms
sections.body: The SOS portal permits renewal in its 30-day pre-expiration and 30-day post-expiration window. That window does not itself extend an expired commission's authority. Review the current assurance, commission approval and stamp date before the next act. Preserve earlier journals under their own retention periods and use the specified notices or transfers when resigning or subject to commission action.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A rural notary plans a trip across the renewal date. Before leaving, the notary checks the filing window, dated education records, exam recency and assurance. If the current term expires before the renewed authority is established, a client appointment cannot supply the missing authority during the gap.

keyFacts: Renewal retains the examination requirement.
A valid assurance must remain on file during authorized work.
Old journal retention survives renewal.

articles.intent: Resolve a Montana notarial work scenario using current official rules
articles.title: Checking Representative Signatures in Montana
articles.description: Separate the appearing person's identity, representative capacity and the notary's own role in the record.
articles.lede: A company packet can involve several different people and roles. The Montana officer must identify which individual is appearing and what that individual claims to do for the entity.

sections.heading: Begin with the individual
sections.body: A community association sends its newly elected treasurer to sign a supplier contract in Helena. MCA 1-5-603(4) still requires the appearing individual's identity to be established through personal knowledge or satisfactory evidence. The association's stationery and general reputation do not themselves identify the particular person at the appointment.

sections.heading: Evaluate the representative claim
sections.body: The same subsection requires a determination about the title or capacity claimed and knowing, willing execution in that capacity for the intended purposes. The permitted sources include the record, the officer's personal knowledge or an official record. The officer may refuse when the presented evidence of capacity is unsatisfactory.

sections.heading: Examine the officer's own participation
sections.body: A company may want the employee who signed for it to notarize the other signer's signature too. MCA 1-5-625(2) expressly addresses a corporate or partnership representative who signs that record or is individually named. In the described prohibited situation, the employee cannot notarize any individual's signature on that record.

sections.heading: Complete the accurate certificate
sections.body: Once the required determinations can be made by an eligible officer, complete the certificate contemporaneously with the act. MCA 1-5-609 requires the act, venue, relevant subject and officer information, signature, date and stamp. The certificate should accurately identify the transaction rather than imply a guarantee of the entity's commercial performance. A separate officer may examine the same supporting material when an employer's signing employee is disqualified, while making that officer's own identity and capacity determinations.

faqs.q: Does the entity's logo identify the signer?
faqs.a: The appearing individual's identity still requires the statutory personal-knowledge or satisfactory-evidence basis.

faqs.q: Can the representative signer notarize the other party on the same record?
faqs.a: Check MCA 1-5-625(2). Its specified representative-signing situation prohibits notarizing any individual's signature on that record.

articles.intent: Resolve a Montana notarial work scenario using current official rules
articles.title: Correcting a Montana Notarial Certificate
articles.description: Use journal evidence, original-officer authority and documented changes when repairing a completed certificate.
articles.lede: A returned document should prompt a controlled review of the original notarial transaction. Montana provides a correction process with specific evidentiary and recordkeeping conditions.

sections.heading: Find the supporting record
sections.body: A county recipient returns an instrument because the acknowledgment certificate omitted a detail. Under MCA 1-5-609(5)(a), a later correction must be evidenced by the original notary's journal record of the transaction. The requested replacement fact must therefore be compared with the transaction record before any change is authorized.

sections.heading: Keep authority with the original officer
sections.body: Only the notary who performed the notarization may make or authorize the correction. A colleague's current commission does not create authority to revise an unrelated officer's certificate. When the original notary authorizes a third party, the authorization must be in writing and the statute's retained-copy requirements apply.

sections.heading: Document the repair
sections.body: The changes must be dated and initialed by the notary, with a corresponding notation in the journal. For an authorized third-party change, attach a copy of the authorizing message and a copy of the changed certificate to the transaction's journal record. These materials explain how the corrected certificate relates to the original act.

sections.heading: Treat the stamp separately
sections.body: The existing official stamp impression or electronic image may not be changed or corrected. The section allows a subsequent proper impression on a tangible record or attachment or logical association of a missing, illegible or incorrect electronic image. MCA 1-5-632 also prohibits unauthorized certificate amendments and reuse of notarial material on another record. The customer can explain the omitted detail, but the original journal must supply the statutory evidence supporting the authorized correction.

faqs.q: Can a client select a more convenient act date?
faqs.a: The change must be supported by the journal record. Client preference alone does not supply that evidence.

faqs.q: Can the old stamp letters be drawn over by hand?
faqs.a: The statute forbids changing the existing stamp image and instead provides the subsequent-impression procedure.

articles.keyword: handling montana requests for notarial records
articles.intent: Resolve a Montana notarial work scenario using current official rules
articles.title: Handling Montana Requests for Notarial Records
articles.description: Apply the different public-access conditions for journal entries and audiovisual recordings.
articles.h1: Handling Montana Requests for Notarial Records
articles.lede: A requester may seek a journal entry, a recording or both. Montana's access rules require attention to the particular record and the legal basis for the request.

sections.heading: Identify an ordinary journal request
sections.body: For ordinary public journal access, MCA 1-5-618(6)(a) calls for a signed tangible or electronic request specifying the month, year, record type and principal. A request to browse all transactions involving an office should be evaluated against those specificity conditions rather than treated automatically as a right to the entire book.

sections.heading: Preserve control and limited disclosure
sections.body: The notary must retain possession or control and provide only the specified entry. The notary also must be satisfied that the request has no criminal or other illegal purpose. A requester who identifies one transaction has not thereby obtained authority to remove pages or retain the original journal overnight.

sections.heading: Use the recording-specific purpose rule
sections.body: Ordinary audiovisual access under subsection (1)(c) similarly requires a signed, specific request and retained original control. Its additional standard is a reasonable purpose directly relating to the notarization. This language should be applied to the recording request on its own terms, even when a related journal-entry request has been made.

sections.heading: Recognize official access categories
sections.body: The statute separately addresses law enforcement officers conducting official investigations, court orders and SOS direction. Those listed official-access categories permit examination and copying without the ordinary restrictions. Preserve the records and respond through the applicable legal route instead of rewriting entries or destroying material after learning that it has been requested. A notary can preserve a copy of the signed request with the response to show the transaction that was identified and the particular record supplied.

faqs.q: Does a request for one entry authorize taking the book?
faqs.a: Ordinary access is limited to the specified entry and the notary must retain possession or control.

faqs.q: Are journal and recording purpose requirements identical?
faqs.a: The recording provision requires a reasonable purpose directly relating to the notarization. The ordinary journal provision addresses criminal or other illegal purpose.

articles.intent: Resolve a Montana notarial work scenario using current official rules
articles.title: Evaluating Overseas Montana Remote Requests
articles.description: Check the foreign-jurisdiction condition, United States record nexus and Montana officer location.
articles.lede: An international signer introduces additional statutory conditions. A successful video connection provides only one part of the Montana remote-notarization analysis.

sections.heading: Locate the officer and principal
sections.body: MCA 1-5-603(10) requires the remote officer to be physically in Montana during the act. The principal may be elsewhere, including abroad when the international conditions are satisfied. A Montana mailing address does not establish the officer's required physical location while traveling in another state.

sections.heading: Establish the required record connection
sections.body: For an overseas principal, the record must involve the specified United States-located matter or entity, United States property, or a transaction substantially connected with the United States. A Montana land agreement provides a clear property subject to examine. Merely placing an unrelated file on a domestic server does not establish the listed substantive connection.

sections.heading: Check the foreign prohibition condition
sections.body: The officer must not know that the act is prohibited in the jurisdiction where the principal is physically located. That condition operates alongside the United States nexus. A client's willingness to pay or request to omit the actual location does not resolve a known prohibition affecting the proposed act.

sections.heading: Apply the session requirements too
sections.body: The ordinary remote safeguards still apply, including satisfactory identity, a single recorded session, record matching, sufficient communication quality and reasonably secure authentication. The principal and required witness must view the same record and the specified record actions occur in real time. The journal, certificate and recording requirements remain part of the completed act. Record the actual location facts used in the international analysis. They affect the statutory eligibility of the session as well as the accuracy of the venue recorded for the Montana officer.

faqs.q: May the officer work from another state during a trip?
faqs.a: The Montana remote provision requires the officer to be physically in Montana at the act.

faqs.q: Does a United States property connection remove every other condition?
faqs.a: The other identity, foreign-prohibition, session, certificate and records conditions still apply.

articles.keyword: leaving a montana employer with notarial records
articles.intent: Resolve a Montana notarial work scenario using current official rules
articles.title: Leaving a Montana Employer with Notarial Records
articles.description: Manage the original journal, employment-related copies and personal stamping device at departure.
articles.h1: Leaving a Montana Employer with Notarial Records
articles.lede: An employer may have purchased supplies and scheduled the notary's appointments. Montana law still assigns specific control and preservation obligations when that employment ends.

sections.heading: Separate payment from device authority
sections.body: MCA 1-5-617 makes the notary the sole owner of the stamping device and responsible for its security. Another individual may not use it for a notarial act or another reason. A department manager therefore cannot treat payment for a stamp as permission for the next employee to use that stamp.

sections.heading: Protect the original journal
sections.body: Under MCA 1-5-618(5), the notary keeps sole control and may not surrender the journal to an employer upon termination without SOS approval. The employer's desire to retain office records should be handled through the actual copy or approved-transfer provisions. Removing pages or concealing the book is not the prescribed transition process.

sections.heading: Identify the employer's copy permission
sections.body: The employer may retain a copy of journal records for acts performed within the scope of employment. A notary who also conducted unrelated weekend acts should identify that scope carefully. The limited copy permission should not be treated as automatic ownership of all originals and all unrelated transactions.

sections.heading: Preserve the later obligations
sections.body: Ordinary journal retention continues for ten years after the last chronicled act, subject to authorized transfer provisions. Resignation also requires notice of the journal's location and triggers the stamp-disabling duty. MCA 1-5-632 independently prohibits intentional withholding of the notary's stamp, journal or commission certificate. A practical departure plan should identify the last chronicled act and any authorized repository arrangement. The retention period follows that record even when the former employer stops operating or changes its records vendor.

faqs.q: Can an employer's successor use the departing notary's stamp?
faqs.a: The notary may not allow another individual to use that device.

faqs.q: May the employer retain employment-related entry copies?
faqs.a: The statute permits those copies while preserving its separate rules for original journal control.

articles.keyword: certified copies and electronic paper copies in montana
articles.intent: Resolve a Montana notarial work scenario using current official rules
articles.title: Certified Copies and Electronic Paper Copies in Montana
articles.description: Distinguish copy accuracy, official-record restrictions and tangible copies of electronic records.
articles.h1: Certified Copies and Electronic Paper Copies in Montana
articles.lede: Copy certification describes the reproduction being compared. The underlying record's category and the officer's relationship to its issuer can determine whether the requested act is permitted.

sections.heading: Establish a complete comparison
sections.body: MCA 1-5-603(5) requires a full, true and accurate transcription or reproduction of the original or official record or item. A private agreement with an omitted signature page cannot be certified as a full copy of the complete agreement. Review what is actually present instead of relying on the requester's label.

sections.heading: Apply the official-record limit
sections.body: MCA 1-5-625(1)(c) restricts certification of copies of official records issued by public entities, with examples including vital records, court records and school transcripts. The stated exception concerns a notary employed by the entity issuing or holding the original version. A general private commission does not by itself satisfy that employment connection.

sections.heading: Understand the electronic-to-tangible route
sections.body: Section 1-5-603(5) expressly permits certification that a tangible copy of an electronic record is accurate. It also addresses a county clerk's acceptance for recording of a tangible copy containing an original notarial certificate. This specific service should be assessed using its actual source record and certificate requirements.

sections.heading: Describe the copy act accurately
sections.body: MCA 1-5-609 requires the certificate to identify the relevant copied record and issuing entity as applicable, along with the other certificate elements. Attach the tangible certificate securely to its record. A copy certification does not itself create the underlying government's original record or guarantee the legal effect of every provision in the copied material. The officer must distinguish examination of the source record from reliance on the customer's verbal assurance that an attachment contains every page.

faqs.q: Can payment remove the official-record restriction?
faqs.a: The statutory employment exception concerns the issuing or original-holding entity. A fee does not create that relationship.

faqs.q: Can Montana certify a tangible copy of an electronic record?
faqs.a: MCA 1-5-603(5) expressly recognizes the accurate tangible-copy service.

articles.keyword: affirmations and directed signatures in montana
articles.intent: Resolve a Montana notarial work scenario using current official rules
articles.title: Affirmations and Directed Signatures in Montana
articles.description: Preserve the principal's intent while using the statutory procedure for physical inability to sign.
articles.h1: Affirmations and Directed Signatures in Montana
articles.lede: Physical difficulty writing and inability to understand a document involve different questions. Montana's directed-signature procedure helps address the former while preserving the officer's substantive determinations.

sections.heading: Identify the participant and intent
sections.body: For an oath or affirmation, MCA 1-5-603(7) requires the officer's identity determination and the participant's knowing and willing statement with intent to be bound. A person who can communicate understanding and intent may still need practical help executing a record. Examine those facts separately rather than assuming one from the other.

sections.heading: Use an eligible directed signer
sections.body: Under MCA 1-5-623, the physically unable principal may direct another individual to sign the principal's name. The individual must be someone other than the notarial officer. The officer's commission does not convert the officer into the designated substitute signer for this statutory procedure.

sections.heading: Keep the explanatory evidence
sections.body: The officer adds the specified notation explaining that the signature was affixed by the other individual at the principal's direction, or words of similar intent. The journal includes the name and address of both the directing principal and the helper. These details explain whose intent and whose physical signing action were involved.

sections.heading: Maintain the refusal boundary
sections.body: MCA 1-5-622 still requires refusal while the officer is unsatisfied about competence, capacity or knowing or voluntary execution. A relative's insistence that a document is urgent does not supply those determinations. The execution accommodation addresses physical inability to sign while preserving the other requirements of the act. The helper's separate name and address in the journal help a later reader distinguish the directing principal from the person who physically wrote the signature at that principal's direction.

faqs.q: Can the notarial officer be the directed signer?
faqs.a: The statute requires an individual other than the notarial officer.

faqs.q: What belongs in the journal for this procedure?
faqs.a: Record both individuals' names and addresses, along with the other required entry details.

articles.title: Quoting Montana Mobile Notary Fees
articles.description: Separate the act fee from additional travel and technology charges before the appointment.
articles.lede: A clear mobile-service quote begins by identifying the act and the additional service. Montana's statute places different conditions on the different parts of that quote.

sections.heading: Identify the actual notarial act
sections.body: MCA 1-5-626(1) lists an up-to-$10 fee for each specified notarial act, including acknowledgments, signature witnessings, jurats, copy or transcript certifications and certification of fact. An officer should determine the services actually performed before counting charges. The statute permits a maximum rather than requiring collection of the maximum.

sections.heading: Explain the additional amount
sections.body: The section permits additional technology or travel charges subject to its conditions and applicable rules. The officer must explain that the amount is additional to the act fee and is an amount not determined by law. A quote should make the nature of that extra service understandable before the customer agrees.

sections.heading: Obtain advance agreement and check the ceiling
sections.body: The requester must agree in advance to the additional amount. Travel fees also must be no more than the IRS standard mileage rates allowed by the statute. Advance agreement therefore does not establish that an otherwise excessive travel charge is permitted. Check the current applicable rate rather than inventing a permanent dollar figure.

sections.heading: Record the completed transaction
sections.body: The journal records the fee, if any, charged by the notary under MCA 1-5-618(3)(h). A free community service still requires the prescribed journal and certificate. A business client paying promptly does not remove the fee cap, the additional-charge conditions or the officer's substantive duties. For a trip with several requested notarizations, identify the number of acts separately from the agreed travel service. The additional agreement cannot increase the statutory maximum charged for any individual act.

faqs.q: Must every listed act cost exactly $10?
faqs.a: The statute permits a fee not exceeding $10 and does not require collecting the maximum.

faqs.q: Can a customer waive the statutory travel ceiling by agreement?
faqs.a: The advance-agreement condition and the stated travel ceiling both apply.

articles.intent: Resolve a Montana notarial work scenario using current official rules
articles.title: Maintaining Record Integrity in Montana Remote Sessions
articles.description: Resolve mismatched records, weak connections and incomplete session evidence before completion.
articles.h1: Maintaining Record Integrity in Montana Remote Sessions
articles.lede: A platform can authenticate a participant while still presenting the wrong version of the record. Montana requires the officer to assess record and session integrity throughout the act.

sections.heading: Confirm the record being used
sections.body: MCA 1-5-603(10)(b) requires satisfaction that the record presented by the principal is the same record remotely notarized. When a lender sends two similar contracts, compare the operative record rather than relying only on a shared filename. The relevant question concerns the record actually signed or acknowledged in the session.

sections.heading: Keep participants aligned in real time
sections.body: The section requires reasonable steps for the principal and required witness to view the same record. Signatures, changes and attachments must occur in real time. A workflow that adds material attachments after participants disconnect should be evaluated against that requirement rather than assumed compliant because the original login succeeded.

sections.heading: Assess the usable connection
sections.body: The officer must be satisfied the communication quality supports the determinations required by notarial law and that access uses reasonably secure authentication. MCA 1-5-622 adds mandatory refusal for unfamiliar or noncompliant technology. A customer's urgency does not improve an inadequate video feed or authorize experimentation with a prohibited workflow.

sections.heading: Preserve the full evidentiary trail
sections.body: Record the entire communication under MCA 1-5-618, and make the separate journal entry with the required technology details and recording location. The certificate identifies communication technology under 1-5-609(3). A short screenshot or a vendor invoice does not substitute for these distinct transaction records. If the quality failure prevents the required determinations, the officer should decline to complete a certificate describing a compliant act. The journal and recording should reflect the transaction actually undertaken.

faqs.q: Do matching filenames establish matching records?
faqs.a: The officer must be satisfied about the actual record, including the version used by the principal.

faqs.q: Does an audiovisual recording replace the journal?
faqs.a: The statute requires the recording and the separate journal entry with its additional technology details.

articles.title: Montana Vehicle Title Changes and Notarial Service Boundaries
articles.description: Apply the 2025 title update without erasing the remaining transfer duties or other notarial restrictions.
articles.h1: Montana Vehicle Title Changes and Notarial Service Boundaries
articles.lede: An old checklist can preserve a requirement that later law removed. Montana notaries should use the current vehicle-transfer provision and distinguish the agency's paperwork from a separate notarial request.

sections.heading: Use the effective change
sections.body: The SOS states that the former transferor-signature acknowledgment requirement for individual-to-individual title transfers was removed effective October 1, 2025. An office should evaluate a stale stamp box or checklist against that official update. The printed existence of an old instruction does not establish that the former requirement remains in force.

sections.heading: Retain the owner's transfer tasks
sections.body: Current MCA 61-3-220 keeps the specified electronic written-authorization route and the tangible title assignment-and-delivery route. The owner must use the applicable procedure for the interest being transferred. Removal of the acknowledgment requirement does not make delivery of an entirely unassigned tangible title the statutory transfer procedure.

sections.heading: Check the transferee's responsibilities
sections.body: The current section describes the transferee's title application and registration routes, generally within its stated 40-day period and subject to the specified exception and cross-references. Its late-compliance provision imposes a $10 penalty in addition to otherwise applicable fees. Those vehicle filing duties have their own triggers and are independent of the notary's renewal calendar.

sections.heading: Respect separate notarial boundaries
sections.body: A request to copy-certify an official title still raises MCA 1-5-625(1)(c) and its employment-based official-record exception. A notary commission also does not guarantee agency approval of a buyer's paperwork. The SOS directs further title-transfer questions to the Title and Registration Bureau, which is the appropriate route for current transaction-specific administrative instructions.
